consent.warningBody: This is a working demonstration rather than a finished product. It does what it says, and the format may still change - so keep anything you would be sorry to lose somewhere else as well.
consent.accept: I have read this and accept it
consent.proceedDisabled: Enter three Spanish words to continue
consent.remember: Don't show this again on this device

clause.noServer: We run no server, and no copy of your lists exists anywhere we control.
clause.gateway: The app itself is delivered through a public IPFS gateway, which sees that you loaded it. Your own Kubo node, or the IPFS Companion extension, fetches it from the network instead.
clause.relay: Relay nodes introduce devices to each other and may keep a copy of a list so another device can collect it later.
clause.sharedList: The list named by the three Spanish words is open: anyone who has those words can read it and write to it. Treat the words as a way to meet, not as a password.
clause.privateList: A list you create yourself decides who may write to it - you, and anyone you let in. It does not decide who may read it.
clause.readingIsOpen: Nothing here is encrypted. Anyone who has a list's address can read everything in it, including the relay that stores it. Do not put anything private in a todo.
clause.identityPasskey: Your passkey identifies you to the other devices. Nobody else can write as you.
clause.identityAnonymous: You are using a random identity that exists only in this browser. Close it and it is gone.
clause.cookies: No tracking cookies are used. If you tick "don't show this again", that choice is the only thing saved on this device.
clause.delegation: You decide who may write to a list, and you can take a grant back later — unlike a key you handed out, because nothing here is encrypted.
clause.storageMemory: You chose "in memory only": nothing is written to this device, and this browser starts over when the page reloads.
clause.storagePersistent: You chose "keep them in this browser": the todos survive a reload. They sit unencrypted in this browser’s storage, and clearing it loses them.

consent.errorNoPasskey: No passkey is stored in this browser, and your authenticator did not hand one over. Create a new one, or continue without one.
consent.errorNeedsLabel: Please give the new passkey a name.
consent.existingNeedsTap: Your passkey asks for a tap on every start. That is why this dialog is back — nothing went wrong.
consent.identityExistingFound: A passkey from an earlier session is stored on this device.
consent.identityExistingNone: Nothing is stored in this browser. We will ask your authenticator, which only works if the passkey carries its own details.
consent.prfMissing: This authenticator cannot carry your identity to a second device (no PRF). The same passkey produces a separate identity there.
consent.mnemonicHelp: Share these three Spanish words to join the same public writable OrbitDB list. This is a share code, not a password or encryption key.
consent.mnemonicSrError: Enter exactly three valid Spanish words.
consent.identityCreateHint: Register a new WebAuthn passkey and derive your OrbitDB identity (DID) from it.
consent.identityCreateHintAnother: Register another WebAuthn passkey — a second identity alongside the one already on this device.
consent.identityAnonymousHint: Use a random per-browser identity, exactly like the previous chapter.
consent.identityLabelHint: Only a label for the passkey picker. Your identity comes from the key, not from this name — two people on this device may use the same one.

element.ok: A direct connection off this network looks possible.
element.unreliable: This network maps a new port per destination and offers no IPv6, so a direct connection usually works only to someone on this same network.
element.none: No path off this network was found. You can still connect to someone on this same network.
element.sameNetwork: Two devices on the same Wi-Fi connect regardless of any of this.
element.details: Show the addresses this check found
element.detailsHint: What a peer would be offered as a route to this device. Turn a VPN on or off and check again - if anything changed, it changed here.
element.detailsDecides: Only the "seen from outside" rows decide the verdict above. The rest are this device’s own addresses, which exist whether or not anything gets out.
element.candidateMdns: Addresses ending in .local are stand-ins the browser substitutes for this device’s own address, so a web page cannot read it. They are not a fault and they are not the VPN.
element.waysHeading: How the other device gets in
element.wayQr: By camera: you hold up a code, they scan it. Nothing leaves this network.
element.relayHint: For when the other device cannot scan your code - over a messenger, for instance. Off unless you ask for it.
element.relayChecking: Looking for a relay that answers…
element.relayNone: No relay answered. Scanning a code still works.
element.privacyHeading: What this means for your data
element.privacyEmpty: The choices above decide what goes here.
element.privacyAccept: I have read this and accept it
technical: A phone closes a waiting invite within seconds of you leaving the app. Only DuckDuckGo and Safari have been seen to hold one for about ten.
Chrome on Android reports no IPv6 where Firefox and DuckDuckGo on the same phone and the same Wi-Fi report one. A verdict describes this browser, not the network.
On mobile data, carrier NAT usually blocks a direct connection to anyone outside that network.
A VPN moves both ends somewhere else, which can fix a blocked network or break a working one.

consent.relayReachable: {count} known relays answered. No directory was queried.
consent.relayDiscovered: {count} relays found in the directory - the ones shipped with this app stayed silent.
consent.storageMemoryHint: Todos and keys live in memory only and are gone on reload. Nothing is left on the device — your identity comes back through the passkey next time, in three touches.
consent.storagePersistentHint: Todos are stored in the browser's IndexedDB and survive a restart. They are not encrypted there, so anyone who can read this browser's storage can read them.

invoice.heading: Invoices
invoice.none: No invoice yet. The first one opens this device's number series.
invoice.needsList: The shared list — the one with the three words — is writable by anyone who knows them. Your invoices and customer addresses would be open to all of them. A list of your own belongs to your identity: only you write to it, and you decide who may see it.

form.issueHint: Issuing assigns the number and freezes the content: from then on it can only be cancelled, not changed.
form.lineDetailsHint: One line each. They appear under the line, and change no figure.

problem.issuerMissing: The settings have no issuer name and address yet.
problem.customerVatId: Reverse charge needs the recipient's VAT id.
problem.deliveryDate: The delivery date is missing — §14 Abs. 4 Nr. 6 UStG asks for it.
problem.noLines: An invoice without a line is not an invoice.
problem.patternCounter: The pattern needs exactly one counter, for example {NNN}.
problem.patternToken: Only {YYYY}, {YY}, {MM} and {N…} are allowed as placeholders.
problem.patternYear: A circle that restarts every year needs the year in the number — otherwise it hands out the same one twice.
problem.patternMonth: A circle that restarts every month needs the year and the month in the number.

note.kleinunternehmer: No VAT is charged, under §19 UStG.
note.reverseCharge: Reverse charge: the recipient owes the VAT (§13b UStG).

settings.heading: Issuer and number series
settings.bankHint: Printed in the footer, and it fills the GiroCode on the invoice.
settings.cryptoHint: Printed in the footer when filled in.
settings.logoHint: PNG, JPEG or SVG. Scaled down to 600 pixels and kept in the list, so every device prints it on the invoice.
settings.logoTooLarge: That image could not be scaled down — please choose a smaller file.
settings.seriesHint: Every identity counts in a series of its own, so two devices can both issue while offline without agreeing on anything — which UStAE 14.5 Abs. 10 allows.
settings.seriesStartHint: Where a series comes from another program, its next number goes here — for example 2026-005.
settings.seriesStartInvalid: That number does not fit this circle's pattern.
settings.patternHint: {YYYY} year, {YY} two digits, {MM} month, {NNN} counter. Everything else stands as written — RE-{YYYY}-{NNN}, for instance.
settings.sharedSeries: Without this identity's digits in the pattern, every device shares one series. That is allowed, and often exactly right for a series carried over — and if two devices issue while both are offline, the app reports the duplicate number rather than renumbering quietly.

document.title: Invoice
document.netNote: Unit prices and amounts are net, in EUR.
document.giroHint: A banking app that scans the GiroCode fills in recipient, IBAN, amount and reference by itself.
document.paymentTerms: Please transfer {amount} by {date} to the account below, quoting invoice number {number} as the reference.

cancelled.confirm: An issued invoice is not changed but cancelled: this writes a cancellation invoice with negative amounts that takes {number} back. Continue?

template.heading: Template for the wording
template.hint: The letter above the lines and the closing under them. A ## heading opens a block, a blank line separates paragraphs, - makes a bullet, **bold** is bold. Placeholders in double braces are filled in when the invoice is issued.
template.unknownHeading: Unknown heading: {names}. That section does not appear on the invoice.
template.unknownPlaceholder: Unknown placeholder: {names}. It stays on the page as written.
template.frozen: An issued invoice keeps the wording it went out with. What you change here applies to the next one.
template.default:
## Letter

Dear Sir or Madam,

thank you for your order. We are charging for the services listed below.

## Closing

Kind regards
{{issuer.managingDirector}}

customers.heading: Customers
customers.none: No customer kept yet. Whoever gets an invoice can end up here — if you want.
customers.deleteConfirm: Remove {name} from the directory? The entry disappears here. It stays in the log, and on every device that already has the list.
customers.deleteHint: A deleted customer disappears from the directory, not from the log: what has been replicated stays replicated. Issued invoices keep their own copy of the address anyway — §147 AO requires it and Art. 17(3)(b) GDPR allows it.
customers.privacyHint: The directory lives in this list. Whoever gets the list gets the directory with it, which is why invoices belong in a list of your own rather than a shared one.

duplicate.banner: Two invoices carry the same number: {numbers}. That happens when one identity issued on two devices while both were offline.
duplicate.keeps: Keeps the number — the customer has it.
duplicate.explain: The invoice that went out first keeps its number, because somebody is already holding it. The later one is cancelled and reissued with the next free number — §31 Abs. 5 UStDV, rather than a quiet renumbering.
duplicate.prepared: The Storno and a copy are waiting as drafts. Both still have to be issued.

invoice.needsListHeading: Invoices need a list of your own
invoice.needsListHint: Under “Lists” → “{action}”. The invoices then live in the same list as that list’s todos.

lists.waiting: Your lists appear here once the app has started.

create.heading: Create a private list
create.hint: Only your identity can write to it. Without a name it gets three Spanish words to recognise it by. Share its address and grant other DIDs below.
create.namePlaceholder: Name of the list — leave empty for three words
create.created: Created {name} — you are now writing to it.
create.share: Share this address so others can open the list. They can read it right away; writing needs a grant below.

switcher.heading: Your lists
switcher.hint: Kept in your own OrbitDB registry, so they come back after a reload and follow your passkey to another device.
switcher.forgetTitle: Remove from this list of lists; the database itself is untouched

open.heading: Open a shared list by address
open.hint: Paste the full OrbitDB address someone shared with you. You can read it right away — writing needs a permission grant from the owner.

permissions.heading: Write permissions
permissions.hint: DIDs allowed to write to this list. Only list admins (the creator) can grant or revoke.
permissions.placeholder: did:key:… of the identity to allow

active.writingTo: You are writing to {name}. The mnemonic below still refers to the public shared list.
active.anyone: Anyone who knows this share code can open the same public database and edit it once connected.
active.replication: The mnemonic selects the same database. Live replication also requires a connection to another browser peer.

form.heading: Add New TODO
form.delegateToggle: Delegate this todo to another DID
form.delegateDidPlaceholder: did:key:… of the person who may complete it
form.delegateHint: The delegate does not get write access to the list. They may only complete or rename this one todo, and you can revoke that at any time.

item.toggleNotAllowed: Only the owner or the delegate of this todo can complete it

networkConfig.label: Network config
networkConfig.description: Validates the configured browser-reachable relay addresses and prepares the libp2p transports and services.

libp2p.label: libp2p
libp2p.description: Creates and starts the libp2p node, including its peer identity, discovery, relay, WebSocket and WebRTC support.

helia.label: Helia
helia.description: Starts the Helia IPFS node on top of libp2p and enables block exchange and HTTP retrieval.

orbitdb.label: OrbitDB
orbitdb.description: Loads or creates the persistent OrbitDB identity and initializes OrbitDB using the Helia node.

databaseSync.label: Database + sync
databaseSync.description: Opens the shared todo database, loads its local operation log and starts OrbitDB pubsub synchronization.

localTodos.label: Local todos
localTodos.description: Connects the local todo store and starts hydrating it from OrbitDB in the background without blocking the application.

relayConnected.label: Relay connected
relayConnected.description: A live WebSocket connection to a relay/bootstrap peer is available for discovery, pubsub and circuit relay traffic.
relayConnected.noOrigin: No HTTPS health URL can be derived from the connected relay address.
relayConnected.loading: Reading the OrbitDB relay version from {origin}/health…
relayConnected.verifiedVersion: OrbitDB relay version {version}; health and peer ID verified at {origin}/health.
relayConnected.verified: Health and peer ID verified at {origin}/health. This relay does not expose its OrbitDB relay version.
relayConnected.unverified: {origin}/health could not be verified, so its OrbitDB relay version is unavailable.

webrtcConnected.label: WebRTC connected
webrtcConnected.description: A live libp2p connection using WebRTC is available. This normally appears after another browser peer has been discovered.

connect.noDialable: No current browser-dialable relays were found.

connect.webrtcDisabled: WebRTC is disabled. Use a relay circuit multiaddress instead.
